title: No final fold against out-breeders: the breeder's mergeRound 499, tested alone after the split gates
hypothesis: On 20 fresh eval maps (seed 880000), both sides, the `breeder` screen opponent (v0024 with splitParentTerritory, splitParentSpace and splitChildSpace 0 and mergeRound 499) beat the champion v0024 22-16-2 (0.575; won both sides on 4 maps, lost both on 1, split on 14); on Default it reached the 64-dragon cap against the champion's 12. Leader 55 splits on 50% of its length-4 turns against our 20% (method.md). A 40-game hint, not proof: test each part alone. This idea changes only mergeRound to 499 (no final fold), on top of whatever the split-gate idea leaves; earlier fold-round results (300 -> 450 -> 415) were on older champions and a different split rate, so they don't settle it.

title: Hunt like the hunter screen entry: hunterMaxLength 5->8, huntMaxDist 6->10 and huntMinEdge 0->-1 together
hypothesis: Opponent model and leader gap (review 1790399621343941000). The `hunter` screen entry is v0018 (65bb229, E0063) with hunterMaxLength 8, huntMaxDist 10, huntMinEdge -1 and mergeRound 100000. Every other entry built on an old champion loses clearly to today's (E0105's screen: v0004 0.26, v0008 0.23, swarm 0.24, folder 0.28, grower 0.07 for the entry), but the hunter plays level with every champion since E0089's: the champion's score against it was 0.39, 0.48, 0.55, 0.50, 0.51, 0.57, 0.52 in the screens of E0089, E0090, E0092, E0099, E0101, E0102, E0105 (100 games each), and v0029 itself scored 0.54. So a bot missing E0089, E0101 and E0102 (+83 between them) keeps up once it hunts widely. The leaders hunt too: head-ons started on longer enemies a game are rank 1 14.3 and the dev benchmark 13.9 against our 5.2 (study.md, submission 6824), and our short heads are within 6 steps of an enemy head of length >= 12 on ~84 dragon-rounds a game from r250 (I235). hunt.hpp is unchanged since v0018 (git diff: a comment only), so the entry's values drop straight onto today's code; the sweep only tries the extremes (group 'hunt any longer head' 20/24/-100, singles 0 and 4x), never these middle values, and I105's SPSA keeps each value's sign, so huntMinEdge -1 is out of its reach. Change: set the three values in bot/params.hpp, nothing else; attackGood, findRam and the protected king are unchanged, so every ram still needs a good trade. Before the SPRT, measure with native.py games on ~40 fresh maps both sides against the champion: head-ons started on longer enemies per game (today ~5), hunting turns per game, and our deaths of length >= 6 dragons; if the change scores <= 0.45 there, also play v0018 with only mergeRound 100000 (the hunter without its hunt values) against v0029 to learn which half carries the entry's strength, and report both. Scenarios (stated through P): a dragon of length P.hunterMaxLength with a visible enemy head twice its length P.huntMaxDist free steps away and one more enemy head than friendly in view walks toward it; boundary: a dragon one longer than P.hunterMaxLength plays normally; the same prey P.huntMaxDist + 1 steps away is ignored; a protected dragon never hunts (attackGood is false). Report the rotation's per-opponent scores, since a wider hunt spends short dragons and the swarm and breeder punish losing count (E0037).
